problem_statement: In a 9-node RPL+TSCH+Orchestra network (built with Orchestra enabled and RPL storing-mode routing), the DAG root does not converge its route table: it never manages to install routes covering the entire network. A scenario that waits for the root to advertise 'Routing entries: 8' (i.e., a route to every other node) times out without that condition being met, so the network cannot be treated as fully reachable even though all nodes are in radio range. The same symptom appears when the network is driven by the existing receiver- and sender-based unicast scheduling rules as well as by the new link-based unicast scheduling rule; in each case the root's routing table is left incomplete and reachability to all nodes is not achieved.
causal_chain: Both upstream Cooja scenarios build the same simple-node application with Orchestra active and assert, via the LogListener/ScriptRunner, that the root node (ID:1) eventually prints 'Routing entries: 8' and then call log.testOK(). Before the fix this condition is never reached within the 6-minute timeout, so the scenario fails; after the production change it is reached and the scenario passes. The assertion depends on TSCH schedule behavior: the production change adds a parameter to tsch_schedule_add_link controlling whether an existing link at the same timeslot/channel is first removed, changes tsch_schedule_remove_link_by_timeslot to clear every matching link (not just one) when the schedule is unlocked, and introduces a new link-based unicast rule whose add/remove path deliberately skips the old-link removal (passing do_remove=0) so that a transmit and receive cell can coexist at the same timeslot on the same channel. The link-based rule also needs a two-address hash to derive timeslot/channel for a node pair. These changes let the unicast cells and the resulting neighbor routes build up correctly so that the root's route table fills to 8 entries, flipping the scenario from fail to pass. The recorded fail-to-pass set is exactly these two scenarios, with no pass-to-pass cases.

verification.reason: The statement clearly describes the convergence symptom and success condition but omits the exact Makefile variable names the test scenarios pass on the build command line and gives no detail about the new link-based rule the agent must create and enable, so a competent developer could not reliably produce the required configuration.

problems.detail: The hidden test .csc files invoke the build with MAKE_WITH_STORING_ROUTING=1 and MAKE_WITH_LINK_BASED_ORCHESTRA=1. The statement describes the concepts ('RPL storing-mode routing' and 'the new link-based unicast scheduling rule') but does not give the exact Makefile variable names the build configuration requires.

The link-based rule is referenced as 'new' but the statement does not name the rule symbol (unicast_per_neighbor_link_based) or describe its scheduling behaviour (pair-based timeslot via a hash of both endpoints' addresses), which the agent must implement and wire into the Orchestra rule list for the link-based test to exercise.

leak_check.leak_detail: The statement reveals much of the fix: exact Makefile variables and CFLAGS behavior, exact Orchestra rule arrays for each configuration, the new public/internal tsch_schedule_add_link do_remove parameter and its required call-site updates, the changed all-matching behavior of tsch_schedule_remove_link_by_timeslot, the new rule name and its scheduling algorithm, and the exact ORCHESTRA_LINKADDR_HASH2 formula. These are implementation details beyond the observable test requirement that the 9-node simulation reaches 'Routing entries: 8'.
leak_check.accuracy_detail: It is largely consistent with the fix but adds many implementation-level requirements that the hidden Cooja tests do not directly check. It also says do_remove=1 preserves current behavior, while the fix changes tsch_schedule_remove_link_by_timeslot to remove all matching links, not just the first one.

problem_statement_fixed: In a 9-node RPL+TSCH+Orchestra network (built with Orchestra enabled and RPL storing-mode routing), the DAG root does not converge its route table: it never manages to install routes covering the entire network. The root never reports 'Routing entries: 8' (i.e., a route to every other node), so the network cannot be treated as fully reachable even though all nodes are in radio range. The same symptom appears when the network is driven by the existing receiver- and sender-based unicast scheduling rules as well as by the new link-based unicast scheduling rule; in each case the root's routing table is left incomplete and reachability to all nodes is not achieved. The network is built from examples/6tisch/simple-node with MAKE_WITH_ORCHESTRA=1 and MAKE_WITH_PERIODIC_ROUTES_PRINT=1, which must accept two new make variables: MAKE_WITH_STORING_ROUTING=1 selects RPL storing-mode routing (and, with Orchestra, the existing RPL-storing unicast rule), and MAKE_WITH_LINK_BASED_ORCHESTRA=1, valid only together with Orchestra and storing mode, selects a new link-based Orchestra unicast scheduling rule instead. In both configurations the root must come to report 'Routing entries: 8'.
